is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles funestus s.s. (page 3, Methods).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study genotypes L119F-GSTe2, 4.3kb-SV, G454A-Cyp9K1, and CYP6P9a (page 5, Methods).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Genotype counts are provided in Figure 4B and the text (e.g., page 6, Results: 'G454A-Cyp9K1 (RR=26/355; RS=4/58; SS=1/32) and 4.3kb-SV (RR=26/301; RS=1/9; SS=0/26)').

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from field sites in Kenya (Busia, Bungoma, Ahero, Kapluk, Kapnarok, Marigiza-Kwale, Taveta, Jaribuni-Kilifi) (page 3, Methods).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study reporting new field collections and genotyping data.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study provides specific site names (e.g., Ahero, Busia, Bungoma, Kapluk, Kapnarok, Taveta, Marigiza, Jaribuni-Kilifi) (page 3, Methods).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collections were conducted between February 2021 and September 2022 (page 3, Methods).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study reports new field collections conducted between 2021 and 2022.

supplement.evidence: The required genotype counts and site information are provided in the main text and figures.

assessment.summary: This study investigated the bionomics, Plasmodium infection rates, and insecticide resistance markers (L119F-GSTe2, 4.3kb-SV, G454A-Cyp9K1, CYP6P9a) in Anopheles funestus populations across different ecological regions in Kenya (Western, Rift Valley, and Coast). It found significant regional differences in resistance marker frequencies and phenotypic resistance, with high pyrethroid resistance intensity in the Rift Valley and Coast, and full susceptibility to bendiocarb and other non-pyrethroid insecticides.
